dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Cephalic tetanus (tetanus infection with localized cranial involvement, likely from an unrecognized head/facial wound in an unvaccinated patient)

Alternatives:
Acute drug-induced oromandibular dystonia (e.g., from dopamine antagonist such as metoclopramide or prochlorperazine, which the patient may not have considered a "medication")
Strychnine poisoning (despite negative toxicology, may be missed if ingestion was remote or testing limited)
Ictal orolingual seizure (focal epileptic event causing sustained jaw and tongue spasm)
